clue.text: Suffering severe blows?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone taking a beating, physical or emotional
setter's reading: the blows are gusts of strong wind battering a place

explanation.surface: Someone is taking a series of heavy punches or setbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The blows are not punches but gales; a place exposed to them is WINDSWEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed terrain lashed constantly by gales is described as being battered by the weather, which matches the cryptic picture.

clue.text: Squeezed by with part of ladder

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
a rung is one of the steps of a ladder

explanation.surface: Someone got pressed against a ladder while passing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wringing out a cloth means twisting and pressing it, so the past tense is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Rotten centre in a fruit

indicators.note: something rotten has broken down, so the following letters fall apart and recombine

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit has gone bad in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten centre' reads naturally as a decayed core, but 'centre in a' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a common stone fruit.

clue.text: Roughly speaking

blocks.note: surface reading: the idiom for approximately
setter's reading: talking in a harsh, grating voice

explanation.walkthrough: The everyday phrase means 'more or less'; read literally it describes a harsh manner of talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is loud and grating, so talking that way is speaking with a rough, harsh tone.

clue.text: Oddly, I see men as adversaries

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange, irregular way, so the letters come out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A speaker confesses they regard men as opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts you to take alternate letters, but here it means strangely: the whole phrase is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Enemies are opponents or foes, people actively hostile to one another.

clue.text: Huge Titian damaged by cold

indicators.note: a damaged painting is knocked out of shape, so the painter's name is rearranged

blocks.note: the Venetian Renaissance painter, taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A huge Titian canvas has been harmed by cold conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means colossal or gigantic, from the Titans, the giant gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: Inspects the luggage

blocks.note: first meaning: to case a place is to look it over, as a burglar does
second meaning: suitcases carried on a journey

explanation.surface: A customs officer looks through the travellers' bags.
explanation.definitionFit: Burglars' slang uses the verb for scouting premises before a raid, and the plural noun means suitcases or bags.

clue.text: Heard to express admiration at masterstroke

indicators.note: heard means we judge by the sound spoken rather than the spelling

blocks.note: to coo is to make soft admiring noises, as over a baby

explanation.surface: People murmur admiringly at a brilliant stroke of play.
explanation.walkthrough: The P of the French word is silent, so it is said the same as the dove's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a brilliant, successful move or stroke, a sense borrowed from French.

clue.text: Extra thin

blocks.note: first meaning: surplus, in reserve
second meaning: lean, without excess flesh

explanation.surface: Something is described as very thin indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra' looks like an intensifier for 'thin'; it is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is a surplus one, and a spare figure is lean or gaunt.

clue.text: Welder set off, but suffered in the heat

indicators.note: set off can mean sent flying or disturbed, so the letters are knocked out of place

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A welder got started on a job but found it unbearably hot.
explanation.definitionFit: To swelter is to be oppressively hot and uncomfortable, so the past tense matches suffering from heat.

clue.text: Untangled clue to start of real medical problem

indicators.note: untangling something knotted changes how its strands lie, so these letters get rearranged
start of asks for only the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of real

explanation.surface: Unravelling a clue leads a doctor to a genuine diagnosis.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is an open sore on skin or a membrane, a genuine ailment a doctor would treat.

clue.text: Two points outrage rebellious followers

indicators.note: rebellious letters refuse to stay in line, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: east and north, two compass points
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple of remarks stir rebellious supporters into fury.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants and hangers-on accompanying a celebrity or important person.

clue.text: Instrument for pardoning a wrong

indicators.note: wrong means not in the right order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A legal instrument is drawn up to forgive an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests a legal document in this surface; it is the musical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand piano is a large keyboard instrument with horizontal strings in a wing-shaped case.

clue.text: Hire charge is split

blocks.note: first meaning: money paid regularly for the use of property
second meaning: torn apart, as a garment

explanation.surface: A rental fee is being shared between people.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenants pay a periodic sum for a property, and the same word as past tense of rend means torn.

clue.text: Masking deception with angelic display

indicators.note: a display spreads things out in a new arrangement, so these letters are laid out afresh

blocks.note: a con is a swindle or trick
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trickster hides their deceit behind a show of innocence.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealing means hiding or covering up, just as a mask hides a face.

clue.text: Father Denis upset one's acquaintances

indicators.note: upsetting something tips it over, so the name's letters land in a new order

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
taken as written

explanation.surface: A priest called Denis has offended the people he knows.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends are the people a person knows and likes, the circle of familiar companions.

clue.text: I ask chefs to cook these

definitions.text: I ask chefs to cook these

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner puts in an order with the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: something a diner might ask chefs to cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishcakes are patties of flaked fish and potato, a dish a customer might ask a kitchen to prepare.

clue.text: Lever first of crates off barrow

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the word that follows
off here means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the opening letter of crates
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone prises the top crate off a wheelbarrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar is an iron bar used to prise things open, a simple example of a lever.

clue.text: Wide group of performers producing radio show

blocks.note: broad means wide
the cast is the company of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A large ensemble puts on a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast is a programme transmitted over the airwaves, such as one on radio.

clue.text: The last to be disturbed by furtive behaviour?

indicators.note: disturbed things are moved from where they were, so these letters are shuffled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sneaking about is the final person anyone expects to be troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is secret, cautious action meant to avoid being noticed, the essence of furtiveness.

clue.text: Had rode off, having stocked up

indicators.note: off here means gone astray, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rider set off on horseback after laying in supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoard is to amass and store supplies, so the past tense means laid in reserves.

clue.text: Trendy bunch who don't like going out?

definitions.text: Trendy bunch who don't like going out?

blocks.note: surface reading: the fashionable clique
setter's reading: a group that stays at home, taken literally

explanation.walkthrough: Fashionable people usually love nights out; the joke reads the first half of the phrase literally, as a crowd that stays in.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an exclusive, fashionable clique of people regarded as socially elite.

clue.text: Authors used to dip into this

definitions.text: Authors used to dip into this

blocks.clueFragment: Authors used to dip into this
blocks.note: surface reading: a book writers browsed through
setter's reading: writers literally dipped their pens in it, in the days of quills

explanation.walkthrough: Dipping into suggests browsing a reference book; 'used to' hints at the old practice of dipping a nib.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pot set into a desk held liquid for pen nibs before fountain and ballpoint pens.

clue.text: Shy actors

blocks.note: first meaning: throw, as in a coconut shy
second meaning: the performers in a play

explanation.surface: Some timid performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like an adjective but is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy a ball is to fling it, as is to cast; the players in a production form the cast.

clue.text: Complain about cutoff point

definitions.note: the verb usually takes 'at': to snipe at someone

blocks.note: a snip is a small piece cut off
east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about where a limit has been set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutoff point' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To snipe is to make sly critical remarks, carping at someone from a safe distance.

clue.text: Bribe sponsor to take in worker

indicators.note: taking in means admitting something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a backer supports a venture financially
a hand is a manual worker, as on a farm

explanation.surface: A sponsor is paid off to employ a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhander is British slang for a bribe, money passed discreetly behind the hand.

clue.text: They wind up at dances

blocks.note: first meaning: spools on which line or film is wound
second meaning: lively Scottish country dances

explanation.surface: Some people end up at dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' suggests finishing somewhere, but here it is winding a line onto a spool.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing line and film are wound on spools, and lively Scottish and Irish folk dances share the name.

clue.text: Sounded frail for a few days

indicators.note: sounded means we go by how the word is said aloud, not its spelling

blocks.note: frail means feeble

explanation.surface: Someone seemed feeble for several days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounded frail' reads as someone's voice being weak; it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven days make up the period, loosely a few days of time.

clue.text: One should be keen at such a critical moment

blocks.note: first meaning: the cutting side of a blade, which ought to be sharp
second meaning: a precarious point where things could go either way

explanation.surface: Advice to stay eager when a crucial time arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' means eager in the surface but sharp in the cryptic reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade's cutting side should be sharp, and the phrase also names a precarious, finely balanced situation.

clue.text: Picture of one playing game

indicators.note: playing with something moves it around, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A photograph of someone taking part in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a visual representation such as a photograph or painting.

clue.text: Bit shy to start with, before kiss

indicators.note: to start with asks for only the opening letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: the opening letter of shy
a peck is a quick light kiss

explanation.surface: Someone was a little bashful at first before kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit shy' reads as 'rather shy'; 'Bit' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A speck is a tiny particle or spot, a minute piece of something.

clue.text: Conference-goers in Leeds get a dance

indicators.note: dancing letters move around the floor and settle in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; Leeds is a city in northern England

explanation.surface: Visitors to a conference in Leeds are treated to a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Delegates are representatives sent to attend a conference or meeting on behalf of others.
